messages:
leah: Noticed a cluster-wide uptick in SSE reconnect churn starting ~03:10 UTC. Pattern: quick close and immediate reconnect, often resume succeeds but users see a flicker. Affected tenants look to be interactive chat routes.
omar: Any correlation with quota enforcement or the new sticky-routing change?
leah: I checked quota logs  no spike in request rate. But proxy trace shows `conn_closed reason=idle_timeout` with idle_ms ~320 and WS peers reporting close code 1001 occasionally.
tessa: 1001 is 'going away' often app-level. Could be our keepalive negotiation got shortened during last runtime tweak. Which flag controls that now?
cory: We merged a change that introduced `sse_keepalive_interval_ms` and defaulted it to 300ms on the assumption shorter keepalives reduce idle sockets. Maybe too aggressive for mobile SDKs.
leah: Action idea: temporary route-level override to set `sse_keepalive_interval_ms=2000` for `/v1/realtime/` and `/v1/chat/` for 10% traffic. Also add a metric `sse.flicker_rate` to console so oncall can see client-visible blips.
omar: Agree. Also adjust reconnect sampling from 0.02 -> 0.15 for those routes so traces will surface SDK behavior. We should limit the increased ingest by only capturing headers+meta unless trace contains `err=resume_failed`.
tessa: On rollouts UX: can the console show both resume_success and resume_latency bucketed by client-version and region? Right now it's buried in logs.
cory: I'll add a temporary panel: group by client_version (from X-RW-SDK header) and region; show 95th resume latency and resume_success_pct. It will be behind a debug tag `sse-flicker-2026-03`.
leah: Also propose: for tenants with reserved capacity, we should add an annotation that 'resume_count' is not billable double-charge unless tokens for overlapping requests are present. Ops should still check `billing.duplicate_resume_tokens`.
omar: For alerting, suggest: alert if `sse.flicker_rate` > baseline*2 for 15m AND resume_success_pct < 98%. That avoids noisy alerts when resumes succeed.
tessa: Can we implement a lightweight client-side SDK instrumentation change too? Add an exponential backoff on immediate reconnect jitter for 500ms +-200ms for first two retries, so UIs don't refetch heavy state immediately. Patch request in SDK repo inbound.
cory: I'll coordinate with SDK team. Quick workaround server-side: if resume_attempts from same client id > 3 in 1s, edge will tag `sse:rapid-reconnect` and we can suppress full tracing to avoid blowing logs.
deploy-bot: rollout "hotfix/keepalive-adjust" started by @ci  routes updated for 10% traffic with tag=sse-flicker-2026-03 :rocket:
leah: Pushed the route patch. Config snippet:
```
- path_prefix: "/v1/realtime/"
  sse_keepalive_interval_ms: 2000
  reconnect_trace_sampling: 0.15
  rollout: {percent: 10, tag: "sse-flicker-2026-03"}
```
omar: I've added the dashboard panel and the alert rule. Linking dashboards here when ready.
tessa: Early telemetry (5m): flicker_rate doubled on canary but resume_success_pct still 99.2%. Not alarming but visible.
cory: Good sign that resume works. Let's keep canary for 2 hours and watch client-version buckets. If flicker is concentrated in older SDKs, plan to release SDK jitter patch and keep server-side override for 24-48h.\leah: If flicker persists and resume_success drops below 97%, we'll rollback the keepalive change cluster-wide.
omar: Also note for future: make keepalive defaults route-scoped rather than cluster-wide to prevent this broad surface. Filing an infra-ops follow-up.
tessa: I'll open the SDK PR with jitter change and link it here.
leah: Thanks all. Please ping in this thread if you see any tenant alerts or if oncall wants escalation. Will update after 2h observation. :eyes:
